hebdo.accroche: The past week saw significant momentum in layered air defence, counter-drone operational deployments, and the historic public disclosure of orbital space weapons. Concurrently, intensifying Houthi ballistic missile strikes on Saudi infrastructure and heightened US-Iran standoff risks compounded strategic strains across Europe and the Indo-Pacific.

tendances.titre: Directed energy and rapid C-UAS integration accelerate across land and naval domains
tendances.resume: Militaries are shifting rapidly from conceptual testing to operational fielding of counter-unmanned aerial systems. South Korea validated a 100 per cent intercept rate for its domestic laser weapon, France trialled the HELMA-P laser aboard the Charles de Gaulle, and the Singapore Army conducted mobile C-UAS field trials. Concurrently, Japan delivered counter-drone suites to Malaysia while the US launched rapid procurement sprints for interceptors and armed surface vessels.

tendances.titre: Integrated air defence recapitalisation deepens amidst acute interceptor stockpile friction
tendances.resume: High-end surface-to-air capabilities saw structural expansion, highlighted by the US activating a dedicated air defence battalion on Guam and France ordering additional SAMP/T NG batteries. However, supply vulnerabilities were laid bare by US delivery holds on Ukrainian Patriot interceptors and severe industrial bottlenecks. In response, nations are prioritising low-cost interceptor development, THAAD component manufacturing ramp-ups, and multinational C2 integration under NATO IAMD initiatives.
